rail_guard.text: Kilkenny Station. Trains for every Irish station you've visited. A nice station, with a nice view of a car park.
Hop aboard. The Wildlore rail runs to any town you have visited on this island. Where to?

then.text: I'm reviewing my KPIs. In particular my KPI for 'not being beaten by a teenager with a rucksack'.
Newgrange is booked for the solstice. Private event. You're not on the list. I checked it twice.

else.text: Kilkenny Castle, grey and tall above the Nore. Director Kerrigan stands on the lawn with an umbrella, a tape measure and a very long list.
Ah. There you are. I was just measuring the Long Gallery. Thirty metres. A lovely Members' Lounge. With a bar.
You'll know Kilkenny's the home of the Cats, of course. The hurlers. They've won a few All-Irelands. I'd like to put them on a fridge magnet.
Regional Director, Ireland. You'll have seen our launch. 'Ireland's Ancient East Experience'. Lanyards included.
Kilkenny Castle would make a lovely Members' Lounge. Shall we discuss it? Battle first, obviously.
She snaps her umbrella shut and tucks it under her arm like a sword being sheathed.
Newgrange is next, in any case. The solstice is the one day of the year when the whole passage fills with light.
The Wardstone will be there. So will I. And I would very much prefer that you weren't.

castle_guide3.text: Kilkenny's 'marble city' name comes from the black limestone that's cut and polished in the quarries nearby. The pavement's the proof.
The castle's been rebuilt a few times. The ghost on the stairs, I'm told, stays out of all the fights.

cat_fan.text: Kilkenny hurling team is called 'the Cats', and they play in black and amber stripes. We've won more All-Irelands than anybody.
If you see a cat statue, salute. If you see a cat in a Dublin jersey, move along.

pub_singer.text: The Medieval Mile's a good walk. Every shop has a long story, and a longer queue.
Mind the Butter Slip. The name's a very honest warning.

marble_worker.text: Kilkenny limestone is dark, hard and full of fossils. It polishes up black as ink. We call it 'marble', and nobody argues.
Look closely at the pavement. There are shells in it, 340 million years old. Walk over them gently.
